issues_discovered.title: Incorrect timestamp conversion causing 1969 epoch dates
issues_discovered.description: event.timestamp was set to (long) (timestamp * 1000) which converted seconds to milliseconds, but TimescaleDBManager.batchInsertAbsorptionEvents expects nanoseconds. This caused all timestamps to become 1969-12-31 19:29:21 (Unix epoch overflow).
issues_discovered.impact: 100% of database inserts failing with duplicate key violations. 0 records in TimescaleDB despite 9,066 events in Redis.

evidence.log_sample: Key (timestamp, symbol, event_type, price)=(1969-12-31 19:29:21.762066-05, MNQZ5, ABSORPTION, 104954) already exists
evidence.error_count: 200+ duplicate key errors in PostgreSQL logs
evidence.affected_records: All absorption events (9,066 in Redis, 0 in DB)

root_cause.problem: timestamp is already in seconds (1.76E9), multiplying by 1000 gives milliseconds (1.76E12), but TimescaleDBManager divides by 1_000_000_000.0 expecting nanoseconds (1.76E18)

fix_applied.explanation: Store original nanoseconds directly. TimescaleDBManager will convert to seconds for PostgreSQL: pstmt.setDouble(1, event.timestamp / 1_000_000_000.0);

issues_discovered.title: Raw Bookmap tick prices not converted to index points
issues_discovered.description: Prices were stored as raw Bookmap tick values (e.g., 105004) instead of index points. For NQ (E-mini NASDAQ), tick prices must be multiplied by 0.25 to get the actual index point value.
issues_discovered.impact: All stored prices are 4x higher than actual market prices. Trading analysis and order placement based on these prices would be incorrect.

root_cause.problem: Direct usage of price from TradeEvent without 0.25 conversion

code_changes.explanation: Apply 0.25 conversion immediately after receiving price from TradeEvent
Preserve original tick value for reference

fix_applied.metadata_addition: Added rawPrice to metadata JSONB: String.format("{\"maxChainSize\":%d,\"rawPrice\":%.2f}", maxChainSize, price)

lessons_learned.lesson: Always verify timestamp units throughout the data pipeline
lessons_learned.context: Mixing nanoseconds, milliseconds, and seconds caused epoch overflow
lessons_learned.prevention: Add unit suffixes to variable names: timestampNanos, timestampMillis, timestampSeconds

lessons_learned.lesson: Instrument-specific price conversions must be applied consistently
lessons_learned.context: NQ requires 0.25 multiplier, ES requires 0.25, other instruments differ
lessons_learned.prevention: Create PriceConverter utility class with instrument-specific logic

lessons_learned.lesson: Silent SQLException failures hide critical issues
lessons_learned.context: Batch inserts failed but application reported success
lessons_learned.prevention: Add explicit error logging and metrics for database operations

lessons_learned.lesson: PostgreSQL logs are invaluable for diagnosing database issues
lessons_learned.context: Duplicate key errors revealed the timestamp bug immediately
lessons_learned.prevention: Monitor PostgreSQL logs proactively in production
